narrative: Round 0 raised a docs parity overclaim (F1) and an eager config read duplicated twice (F2/F3), all valid and fixed well in 1ac3448. F1's fix covered the ls paragraph and CHANGELOG but missed a third statement of the same parity claim in the backlog section, which round 1 caught as F4. Round 2's F5 was an uncertain edge case on original code; the agent split it correctly, taking the test and docs and refuting the filter by mutation.
guidance_observations: The agent's class sweeps were wording-based on the first pass and claim-based only after the reviewer found a missed site; a claim-based sweep at the F1 fix would have saved round 1.
Mutation-testing the reviewer's proposed alternative (F5) turned a preference disagreement into evidence, which is the right shape for a pushback.

narrative: Round 0 found a class of stale 30s/300 restatements (F1-F3, F5), a mis-paired median (F4), and a real broken invariant (F6). The fixes created most of what followed. F6's aggregate bound left out terms one at a time: the sleep (recovered from a review that failed to post), then the engine close (F13). Its pin had a thin flake margin (F9). The citation sweep claimed full coverage but missed sites (F8) and then introduced a wrong identifier (F12). F7 was CHANGELOG drift from shortening the message in response to the unposted finding. F10 and F11 were original-code instances of the PR's own one-source-of-truth thesis that round 0 missed.
guidance_observations: Two of the fix-caused findings (F7 and the sleep term) trace to a review on 0f31eae that failed to post and was recovered from the artifact; those findings have no thread, so chains through them are invisible to per-finding attribution.

The agent's verification kept being scoped to what it had edited rather than what its edit invalidated, as it says itself in F8 and F12; a whole-file citation resolver run before the first fix push would have closed F8 and F12 together.
Every pushback-shaped choice (F4 different fix, F6 remedy choice) was argued with arithmetic and was correct.
